Cournot Oligopoly

Each firm picks its best output against its rivals' — the reaction functions cross at the Cournot-Nash equilibrium. Push the firm-count NNN slider: at N=1N = 1N=1 it is monopoly, and as NNN grows it converges to competition.

Examples & Exercises

In a duopoly with demand P=10−QP = 10 - QP=10−Q and c=2c = 2c=2, derive each firm's reaction function and compute the Cournot-Nash equilibrium by hand.

q1=A−c−q22,q2=A−c−q12q_1 = \frac{A - c - q_2}{2}, \qquad q_2 = \frac{A - c - q_1}{2}q1​=2A−c−q2​​,q2​=2A−c−q1​​
Show proof
  1. Firm 1's profit is (10−q1−q2−2)q1(10 - q_1 - q_2 - 2)q_1(10−q1​−q2​−2)q1​. Differentiating in q1q_1q1​: 8−2q1−q2=08 - 2q_1 - q_2 = 08−2q1​−q2​=0, so q1=(8−q2)/2q_1 = (8 - q_2)/2q1​=(8−q2​)/2. Symmetrically, q2=(8−q1)/2q_2 = (8 - q_1)/2q2​=(8−q1​)/2.
  2. By symmetry q1=q2=q∗q_1 = q_2 = q^*q1​=q2​=q∗: q∗=(8−q∗)/2q^* = (8 - q^*)/2q∗=(8−q∗)/2, so q∗=8/3q^* = 8/3q∗=8/3. Total output Q=16/3Q = 16/3Q=16/3 and price P=10−16/3=14/3≈4.67P = 10 - 16/3 = 14/3 \approx 4.67P=10−16/3=14/3≈4.67 — between the monopoly price 666 and the competitive price 222.

Show that the Cournot model gives the monopoly solution at N=1N = 1N=1 and converges to the competitive outcome as N→∞N \to \inftyN→∞. Compute the numbers for N=8N = 8N=8.

QN=NN+1A−cB,PN=A+NcN+1Q_N = \frac{N}{N+1}\frac{A-c}{B}, \qquad P_N = \frac{A + Nc}{N+1}QN​=N+1N​BA−c​,PN​=N+1A+Nc​
Show proof
  1. At N=1N = 1N=1, Q1=12A−cBQ_1 = \frac{1}{2}\frac{A-c}{B}Q1​=21​BA−c​ and P1=A+c2P_1 = \frac{A+c}{2}P1​=2A+c​ — exactly the monopoly solution. As N→∞N \to \inftyN→∞, QN→A−cB=QcQ_N \to \frac{A-c}{B} = Q_cQN​→BA−c​=Qc​ and PN→cP_N \to cPN​→c — the competitive outcome.
  2. At N=8N = 8N=8: Q=89⋅8=64/9≈7.11Q = \frac{8}{9}\cdot 8 = 64/9 \approx 7.11Q=98​⋅8=64/9≈7.11, P=10+169=26/9≈2.89P = \frac{10 + 16}{9} = 26/9 \approx 2.89P=910+16​=26/9≈2.89. With just 8 firms the price is already close to marginal cost 222 — how the Cournot model shows competition as the limit in the number of firms.
